Sanjay — great questions, appreciate the clarity. Quick recap and next steps: 

1) SDK/API parity: Redwood supports an OpenAI-compatible surface and we provide language SDKs (Node, Go, Python). We can run a smoke test where you point a small service at Redwood and exercise the same calls — this usually surfaces any prompt/formatting diffs quickly.
2) Private deployment: we offer a VPC option with customer-managed KMS and audit logs. Dylan can share the deployment diagram and standard SOC2 evidence.
3) Hyperscaler comparison: we recommend a three-phase eval — parity test (API/outputs), perf test (p90/p99 latency under load), and cost test (token/unit cost with batching). I attached a migration checklist and a short prompt diff doc to get started.

Proposed next steps:

- Prompt diffs: attached prompt-diff-examples.md with before/after pairs. Common items: tokenizer edge cases for non-UTF punctuation, stop-sequence behavior, and subtle temperature sampling differences. We include a small harness that can run both endpoints against a prompt set and produce a diff report.

Sanjay — thanks, confirmed Wed 2026-04-15 09:00 PST. Quick competitive summary I’ll bring to the call (preview):

- Latency (p99): Redwood’s runtime targets sub-200ms p99 for 256-token interactive workloads on our Dedicated configs; production numbers vary by model size and hardware. Hyperscalers typically have comparable raw latency but different batching and multi-tenancy behaviors — we can pin fixed-capacity nodes for more predictable p99s.
- Batching & cost: Redwood exposes batching knobs (max batch size, latency budget) to trade cost vs latency deterministically; hyperscalers handle batching internally and that can create variance at peak. This is a common migration consideration.
- API compatibility: We support the OpenAI-compatible surface and provide SDK shims for minimal code changes. Caveats: model alias mapping, streaming chunk boundaries, and a few edge tokenizer differences (covered in prompt-diff doc).

Deliverables uploaded to drive: perf harness (runnable script), migration checklist, prompt diffs, and the SDK swap guide. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/FinCo/migration-notes.

See you on the call — I’ll record action items and next tests (parity run + 5-minute perf sweep + cost calc).

Best,
Marissa
